# windows_power_plan (Resource)

Manages the active power plan of a remote Windows machine over SSH/PowerShell.

The active plan is a **singleton**: the host always has exactly one, so creating this resource never provisions anything new — it only writes the configured AC/DC setting values in place (`powercfg /setacvalueindex` / `/setdcvalueindex`) and activates the plan (`powercfg /setactive`), and deleting it makes no remote change unless `restore_on_destroy` is set.

`plan` takes a GUID or an alias (`balanced`, `high_performance`, `power_saver`, `ultimate_performance`), normalised to the canonical GUID at plan time. Plan names are never accepted: `ElementName` is localised. When the desired plan is absent from the host (e.g. `ultimate_performance`), `create_if_missing` duplicates the well-known template (`powercfg /duplicatescheme`); custom plan GUIDs have no template source and still fail with `plan_not_found`. Otherwise a missing plan is an error. Only the listed `settings` are managed. Identity is GUID-only everywhere: `powercfg /query` text is never parsed.

**Destroy is a no-op by default:** a Windows machine cannot exist without an active plan; `terraform destroy` only removes the resource from state unless `restore_on_destroy` re-applies the pre-existing plan and values. A plan duplicated by `create_if_missing` is deleted on destroy whenever it is inactive (`powercfg /delete`).

Import format: any non-empty ID (its value is ignored; the live active plan is adopted, e.g. `current`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Minimal example: switch the target host to the High performance plan and
# never spin the disk down on AC power. The active plan is a singleton —
# this resource activates it in place and never provisions anything new.
# Destroy is a no-op unless restore_on_destroy re-applies the pre-existing
# plan and values captured at creation time.
resource "windows_power_plan" "this" {
  plan = "high_performance"

  settings = [
    { subgroup = "SUB_DISK", setting = "DISKIDLE", ac_value = 0 },
    { subgroup = "SUB_SLEEP", setting = "STANDBYIDLE", ac_value = 0, dc_value = 0 },
  ]

  restore_on_destroy = true

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly: without this block each
  # operation defaults to 5 minutes, and a stalled powercfg or read-back
  # surfaces a timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform
  # indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "5m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "5m"
    delete = "5m"
  }
}

output "plan_guid" {
  value       = windows_power_plan.this.plan_guid
  description = "Resolved GUID of the active power plan."
}

output "plan_name" {
  value       = windows_power_plan.this.plan_name
  description = "Localised display name of the active power plan."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `plan` (String) Desired active power plan: a GUID or an alias (`balanced`, `high_performance`, `power_saver`, `ultimate_performance`). Normalised to the canonical GUID at plan time. Plan names are localised and never accepted.

### Optional

- `create_if_missing` (Boolean) When `true`, duplicate the plan template on the host (`powercfg /duplicatescheme`) when the desired plan is absent. Only well-known template GUIDs (`balanced`, `high_performance`, `power_saver`, `ultimate_performance` aliases) can be duplicated; arbitrary custom plan GUIDs have no template source and still fail with `plan_not_found`. Defaults to `false`: a missing plan is an error. The duplicated plan is deleted on destroy whenever it is inactive.
- `restore_on_destroy` (Boolean) When `true`, destroy re-activates the plan that was active at creation (or import) time and restores the captured setting values. Defaults to `false`: destroy makes no remote change.
- `settings` (Attributes List) Power setting overrides applied to the selected plan, in order. Only listed settings are managed; every other setting is left untouched. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings))
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Terraform resource ID. Equal to the host `MachineGuid` (`HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography\MachineGuid`). Stable across power plan changes.
- `plan_guid` (String) Resolved GUID of the active power plan as observed on the host.
- `plan_name` (String) Localised display name (`ElementName`) of the active power plan as observed on the host. Informational only: never used for identity or drift.

<a id="nestedatt--settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `settings`

Required:

- `setting` (String) Setting: a GUID or `powercfg` alias (`STANDBYIDLE`, `HIBERNATEIDLE`, `DISKIDLE`, `VIDEOIDLE`, `PROCTHROTTLEMIN`, ...). Resolved on the host via `powercfg /aliases`.
- `subgroup` (String) Setting subgroup: a GUID or `powercfg` alias (`SUB_SLEEP`, `SUB_DISK`, `SUB_PROCESSOR`, `SUB_VIDEO`, `SUB_BUTTONS`, ...). Resolved on the host via `powercfg /aliases`.

Optional:

- `ac_value` (Number) Setting value when on AC power (setting index, `>= 0`). At least one of `ac_value` or `dc_value` is required per setting. DC values are stored even on hosts without a battery.
- `dc_value` (Number) Setting value when on DC (battery) power (setting index, `>= 0`). At least one of `ac_value` or `dc_value` is required per setting. Stored even on hosts without a battery.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import the live active power plan of the target Windows host.
# The active plan is a singleton, so any non-empty import ID is accepted and
# ignored: the live plan is adopted and becomes the snapshot for a later
# restore_on_destroy.
terraform import windows_power_plan.this current
```
